touches.text: The abstract ticket owns what every kind shares: its birth (cast) and its three parts, each with one job: the plan (only what a builder builds from), the metadata and state (what gates and doors read and write as it moves), and the history (the append-only log). WHY: one job per part reduces confusion; a builder reads the plan and nothing else.
Coding Ticket: what we usually mean.
Lives in CairnCommons/tickets/ while staged; its trail migrates beside its code as that component's history while under way, and back to the commons after (Law 5).

Outline check: when a ticket is cast, the cheapest model reads it beside the outline sections it touches. A conflict, or an open question in those sections, becomes a question on the ticket, which holds its build until answered. It reads the outline as it stands each time, so editing the outline costs nothing.

A ticket's plan carries only what a door can check. A decision line's by (free prose, census 2026-09-16: 70 of 70) is not checked and not kept: the cast door checks writes_to and reads, and by goes. Who authored a line is not tracked (Akien 2026-10-28: "there is no point in tracking the 'authoring entity'", except a gate-pass certificate). CC's decision, 2026-11-13, on Q#96 (ticket d421051bc1f7, child C), after Akien: "we are moving away from prose. that's why the tickets became json ... we need things we can check. and that does mean you have to create adjudications. but i'd say this one isn't working."
Seals: one current validation per proof, beside the proof. A seal holds while the code it measured is unchanged.

Commit: the proofs of the component the ticket changed, since RULE 1 bounds a change to its component. Passing them puts the component in service, yellow: proven where it changed, not yet measured against what depends on it. Akien: "being put in service only requires that it's the best we can do now. only requires 80% trust."

artifact: the one door a record of truth changes through, and the journal of who came through it (hash-chained, caller read from the kernel). WHY: errors are permanent in records of truth (Law 7), and the journal is what shows a record moved by hand. USERS: everyone who writes a record.
charter: compiles a component's bounded state from its history. WHY: state is compiled from the component's tickets, never hand-edited (Law 5). Held by CodeMother.
